title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its commitments to strengthen AI governance and ensure accountability, safety, and transparency. It details measures such as new regulatory frameworks, standards development, and collaboration with industry and academia to uphold public trust in AI.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has outlined how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector to protect exam integrity and fairness. The policy aims to set clear rules and standards for AI applications in assessments, responding to government requests for guidance.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how artificial intelligence systems use copyrighted works and evaluates the legal, ethical, and societal implications of that practice. It offers impact assessments and policy recommendations to guide responsible AI development and use of copyrighted content.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government outlines its response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, reaffirming its commitment to harness AI's benefits while addressing risks. It details plans for regulation, investment in research, and international cooperation to ensure the technology is developed responsibly and ethically.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document defines the scope, responsibilities, and decision‑making framework for a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence should be governed by public standards, clarifying its objectives and expected outcomes. It also includes a FAQ section that explains the committee’s purpose, the review process, and ways for stakeholders to participate and stay informed.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence, outlining their views and concerns about AI regulation. Their submission focuses on how AI should be governed to balance innovation with safety and ethical considerations.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence shapes the regulation of medical products, looking at new AI tools and how they fit into current regulatory systems. It applies the principles from the AI White Paper to ensure that AI‑driven medical devices are safe, effective, and ethically used.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This policy outlines the Defence's plan to become the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential organization in AI for its size. It emphasizes a vision of leadership in AI capabilities and influence across the defense sector.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will work with the transport sector to harness the benefits of AI. It also outlines measures to mitigate potential risks and ensure safe, responsible deployment.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This progress report examines how AI systems are built using copyrighted materials and evaluates compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights recent developments, challenges, and recommended best practices for lawful data usage in AI.
